script.problem: It uses a reaction phrase. The code shows reactions; the explanation never does.

terra.problem: The verse says Hoshea did evil, but not like the kings before him. It does not specify that he did less evil.
The landlord comparison invents a request for a guest room and does not match the action of conspiring to send envoys.
“Prison came first” places the arrest before the next year, but the text gives no such timing.
“Nobody got a ticket to Egypt” suggests nobody went there. The text does not say whether the envoys went.
Comparing a three-year siege to waiting for cookies to cool makes light of a violent situation.
“He stayed” presents the king as personally remaining at Samaria throughout the siege. The text does not say that.
“The king of Assyria staying put at Samaria” presents him as personally remaining there throughout the siege, which the text does not state.
Calling Samaria Israel's capital adds a Bible fact not stated in this passage without a supporting reference.
The text says Hoshea had conspired to send envoys to King So. It does not say he had reached out to him.
“Nobody drove him anywhere” makes a broader claim than the passage supports.
“Every hill” drops the verse's qualification that they were high hills.
The cookie-mold joke makes light of Israel's idol-making, a serious sin in the passage.
“That's the answer the card wants” refers to the lesson card rather than speaking naturally about the passage.
Calling Ephraim a tribe adds a Bible fact not stated in this passage without a supporting reference.
Calling Dan a tribe adds a Bible fact not stated in this passage without a supporting reference.
“It wasn't a surprise” asserts how people experienced the event. The text says it had been declared through the prophets, not whether anyone was surprised.
